description: The root lens and its six second-layer ideas, revealed by tapping Entropy a second time. The eight entrances are defined in their own clusters.

concepts.title: Entropy
concepts.summary: Energy spreads. Order is something the universe can make locally, but never maintain for free. Almost everything I find beautiful leans on that bargain: heat leaving, structure forming, time refusing to run backward.

concepts.title: Arrow of Time
concepts.summary: The small laws mostly run either way. Time gets its direction from large numbers: ice melts, coffee cools, memories pile up. The reverse isn't forbidden, only overwhelmingly improbable.

concepts.title: Decay & Renewal
concepts.summary: Nothing holds its shape for free. Yet what falls apart becomes the ground for what comes next. Decay isn't the opposite of growth; it's the other half of the same cycle.

concepts.title: Local Order
concepts.summary: A crystal, a cell, a city. Order can grow wherever there's somewhere else to send the disorder. Every island of structure is paid for by warming the water around it.

concepts.title: Information
concepts.summary: Entropy also measures what you don't yet know. The more ways a system could be arranged, the more a single answer is worth. Uncertainty turns out to be something physical.

concepts.title: Waste Heat
concepts.summary: Useful motion always leaves some warmth behind. Engines, chips, bodies: each turns a little order into a little heat, then hands that heat back to the world.

concepts.title: Emergence
concepts.summary: Complexity can still appear in a universe drifting toward spread-out. When energy flows through matter, patterns lock in: storms, cells, minds. Each one is a temporary answer to a steady push.
